rationale:
The subject requires the review prompt to give a report template with four sections: revised text of the group's requirements, including new split ones, as complete directives ready to paste; revised text of outside requirements the changes affect; mechanical changes, including new full names and added examples; and design questions.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_review_prompt_gives_a_report_template]` takes the `## Report` section of the review prompt. It does this through `section(review_prompt(), "## Report")`. `review_prompt` reads `references/review-prompt.md` of the habeas-requirements skill. The test then calls `assert_text_in_order`, which fails if any phrase is missing or out of order. The phrases map to the four sections:
- `### Revised text`, then "as complete directives ready to paste, including new split requirements", covers section 1.
- `### Edits outside the group`, then "revised text of other requirements your changes make stale", covers section 2.
- `### Mechanical changes`, then "list new full names and added examples", covers section 3.
- `### Design questions` covers section 4.

The heading and descriptive phrase for each section are both asserted, and `assert_text_in_order` also enforces their order. The `section` helper limits the search to the Report section, so matches elsewhere in the prompt cannot satisfy it. Nothing asserts the literal "every requirement in the group" wording. The "ready to paste" and "new split requirements" phrases carry the substance of that bullet, so I don't count this as a gap. No acknowledgments apply.

text: The review prompt MUST give a report template with these sections:
- the revised text of every requirement in the group, including new split requirements, as complete directives ready to paste;
- the revised text of requirements outside the group that the changes affect;
- the mechanical changes, including new full names and added examples;
